newsitem.title: USA: Conn. voters want more money for colleges - survey.
newsitem.headline: Conn. voters want more money for colleges - survey.

text.p: Connecticut voters overwhelmingly favor plans to beef up support for state universities and to help parents and students pay for college education, according to a poll released on Wednesday.
But the Quinnipiac College Poll also found that state voters were evenly split on whether they would pay higher taxes to fund state universities.
By a 91 to seven percent margin, Connecticut voters support tax credits for tuition payments.
Some 71 percent favor increased state funding to state universities, and 76 percent approve of increased state funding of student financial aid.
By a 73 to 22 percent margin, voters said Republican Governor John Rowland's proposal to cut state spending for state universities by 10 percent was a "bad idea."
The poll was concluded before Rowland amended his plan to a possible cut of six percent.
Asked if they would be willing to pay more taxes to avoid a cut to state universities, 49 percent said yes, and 46 percent said no -- a statistical tie.
The poll has a margin of error of plus or minus three percent.

"While Connecticut voters overwhelmingly support more state spending for higher education, there is a great deal of reluctance to pay more taxes for anything," said Douglas Schwartz, director of the Quinnipiac College Poll.

"While voters are split on the specific question of whether they would pay more taxes to support higher education, in more general questions about taxes, voters have been saying two to one, cut them," Schwartz said.
Quinnipiac College surveyed 1,059 Connecticut residents who said they were registered voters. The poll was conducted Feb 18-23.
